spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m1p1t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS N, MaxBatch

ASSUME N \in Nat /\ N >= 2 /\ MaxBatch \in Nat

Engines == 1 .. N

VARIABLES holder, tally, committed

vars == << holder, tally, committed >>

Init ==
    /\ holder = 1
    /\ tally = 0
    /\ committed = [e \in Engines |-> 0]

Sum[S \in SUBSET Engines] ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE
         IN committed[x] + Sum[S \ {x}]

Commit ==
    /\ committed[holder] < MaxBatch
    /\ tally' = tally + 1
    /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![holder] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED holder

PassToken ==
    \E m \in Engines :
        /\ m # holder
        /\ holder' = m
        /\ UNCHANGED << tally, committed >>

Next == Commit \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdates == tally = Sum[Engines]
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    N = 3
    MaxBatch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction where several matching engines share one consolidated order-book tally. To avoid two engines clobbering each other's writes, the engines are arranged in a logical ring and pass a single write token around; only the engine currently holding the token may add its accumulated orders into the shared tally. Because the ring runs over an unreliable bus, the token-handoff messages can be reordered, so the token may arrive at any other engine next rather than strictly the ring successor. Each engine keeps a private count of how many order batches it has folded into the tally. Every time the token holder commits, it increments the shared tally by one and bumps its own private count by one. The only way the shared tally could diverge from reality is if an update were lost or double-counted. We want to guarantee the consolidated tally always exactly reflects the sum of what every engine has committed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared order-book tally always equals the sum of the per-engine committed batch counts, so no engine's update is ever lost or overwritten.

spec_text:
--------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m9p2t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Fleet, MaxEpoch

ASSUME Fleet \in Nat /\ MaxEpoch \in Nat

Sectors == {"north", "south"}

VARIABLES reserve, transit, patrol, epoch

vars == << reserve, transit, patrol, epoch >>

Init ==
    /\ reserve = Fleet
    /\ transit = 0
    /\ patrol = [s \in Sectors |-> 0]
    /\ epoch = 0

Launch ==
    /\ reserve > 0
    /\ reserve' = reserve - 1
    /\ transit' = transit + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << patrol, epoch >>

Settle ==
    \E s \in Sectors :
        /\ transit > 0
        /\ transit' = transit - 1
        /\ patrol' = [patrol EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
        /\ UNCHANGED << reserve, epoch >>

Recall ==
    \E s \in Sectors :
        /\ patrol[s] > 0
        /\ patrol' = [patrol EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1]
        /\ reserve' = reserve + 1
        /\ UNCHANGED << transit, epoch >>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << reserve, transit, patrol >>

Next == Launch \/ Settle \/ Recall \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DroneConservation == reserve + transit + patrol["north"] + patrol["south"] = Fleet
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Fleet = 3
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DroneConservation
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm keeps a fixed fleet of aerial drones that are either parked in a ground reserve, in transit between locations, or actively patrolling one of several fire sectors. Command reconfigures the swarm in numbered epochs: when conditions change it bumps the epoch and may relaunch, land, or recall drones to rebalance coverage. A drone launched from the reserve first enters a transit state before it settles into a sector, and a recalled drone returns to the reserve. Crucially, drones in this model are never destroyed or spontaneously created; a drone that is slow to respond is still somewhere in the fleet, just in transit rather than lost. Command must always be able to account for every airframe it owns. If the books ever failed to balance, it would mean a drone had been silently dropped or duplicated.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the reserve count plus the in-transit count plus the number of drones across all sectors always equals the fixed total fleet size.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m5p0t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Teams, Board, Quorum

ASSUME Quorum \in Nat

VARIABLES occupied, ballot

vars == << occupied, ballot >>

Support(t) == { m \in Board : ballot[m] = t }

Init ==
    /\ occupied = {}
    /\ ballot = [m \in Board |-> "none"]

CastVote ==
    \E m \in Board, t \in Teams :
        /\ ballot[m] = "none"
        /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![m] = t]
        /\ UNCHANGED occupied

Enter ==
    \E t \in Teams :
        /\ occupied = {}
        /\ Cardinality(Support(t)) >= Quorum
        /\ occupied' = {t}
        /\ UNCHANGED ballot

Release ==
    \E t \in Teams :
        /\ t \in occupied
        /\ occupied' = occupied \ {t}
        /\ ballot' = [m \in Board |-> "none"]

Next == CastVote \/ Enter \/ Release

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AtMostOneTeamInRoom == Cardinality(occupied) <= 1
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Teams = {t1, t2}
    Board = {b1, b2, b3}
    Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOneTeamInRoom
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler governs one shared operating room that only a single surgical team may occupy at a time. Before a team may enter, it must collect approving votes from a quorum of the scheduling board members; only once it holds a majority of votes may it seize the room. Votes travel over an internal messaging fabric that can reorder them, so a team may accumulate its approvals in any order. When an occupying team finishes, it releases the room and the votes are cleared for the next contest. The absolute requirement is that the physical room never holds two teams simultaneously, no matter how votes are reordered or interleaved.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at no point are two different surgical teams simultaneously occupying the operating room.

spec_text:
--------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m4p5t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
CONSTANTS Jobs, Capacity

ASSUME Capacity \in Nat /\ Capacity >= 1

VARIABLES queue, printed, alive

vars == << queue, printed, alive >>

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ printed = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]
    /\ alive = TRUE

Enqueue ==
    \E j \in Jobs :
        /\ Len(queue) < Capacity
        /\ queue' = Append(queue, j)
        /\ UNCHANGED << printed, alive >>

PrintHead ==
    /\ alive
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ LET j == Head(queue) IN
        /\ printed[j] = 0
        /\ printed' = [printed EXCEPT ![j] = 1]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED alive

DropDuplicate ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ printed[Head(queue)] = 1
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED << printed, alive >>

Crash ==
    /\ alive
    /\ alive' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED << queue, printed >>

Recover ==
    /\ ~alive
    /\ alive' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED << queue, printed >>

Next == Enqueue \/ PrintHead \/ DropDuplicate \/ Crash \/ Recover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PrintedAtMostOnce == \A j \in Jobs : printed[j] <= 1
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Jobs = {j1, j2}
    Capacity = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PrintedAtMostOnce
nl:
A print shop runs a spooler in front of a single physical printer. Incoming print jobs are appended to a bounded spool queue; when the queue is full the intake applies backpressure and refuses new jobs rather than dropping anything. A worker pulls the head job off the queue and sends it to the printer, which is an irreversible physical act: paper and toner are consumed, so a job must never be printed twice. To track this the spooler keeps, for every job id, a counter of how many times it has actually been sent to the printer. The worker can crash silently at any moment and simply stop pulling jobs, which is fine for safety as long as it never re-prints. We care that no physical page is ever produced twice for the same job.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every job has been sent to the printer at most once, so no print-count ever exceeds one.

spec_text:
--------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m2p6t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Locks, MaxRound

ASSUME MaxRound \in Nat /\ MaxRound >= 1

VARIABLES round, voted, unlocked, decided

vars == << round, voted, unlocked, decided >>

Init ==
    /\ round = 1
    /\ voted = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ unlocked = FALSE
    /\ decided = 0

CastVote ==
    \E l \in Locks :
        /\ voted[l] < round
        /\ voted' = [voted EXCEPT ![l] = round]
        /\ UNCHANGED << round, unlocked, decided >>

Commit ==
    /\ ~unlocked
    /\ \A l \in Locks : voted[l] = round
    /\ unlocked' = TRUE
    /\ decided' = round
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, voted >>

Relock ==
    /\ unlocked
    /\ unlocked' = FALSE
    /\ decided' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, voted >>

NewRound ==
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ unlocked' = FALSE
    /\ decided' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED voted

Next == CastVote \/ Commit \/ Relock \/ NewRound

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleUnlock == unlocked => (\A l \in Locks : voted[l] = decided)
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Locks = {front, back}
    MaxRound = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleUnlock
nl:
A smart-home security system controls a network of door locks that must all release together during an authorized exit, coordinated by a two-phase commit. A coordinator opens a numbered unlock round and each lock is a participant that must cast a vote stamped with the current round number. The coordinator may only commit the unlock once every lock has voted in the current round; a lock whose most recent vote belongs to an earlier round is considered stale and must re-vote before it counts. Locks can be slow to answer but never fail outright, so a tardy lock simply has not voted yet in this round. When the coordinator starts a fresh round it advances the round number, which instantly makes all prior votes stale. The safety concern is that the doors must never be reported as committed-unlocked on the strength of a stale participant's old vote.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the network is in the committed-unlocked state, every lock's recorded vote belongs to the exact round in which the unlock was decided.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m9p5t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Containers, MaxEpoch

ASSUME MaxEpoch \in Nat

VARIABLES lifts, epoch

vars == << lifts, epoch >>

Init ==
    /\ lifts = [c \in Containers |-> 0]
    /\ epoch = 0

NormalLift ==
    \E c \in Containers :
        /\ lifts[c] = 0
        /\ lifts' = [lifts EXCEPT ![c] = 1]
        /\ UNCHANGED epoch

AdminForceLift ==
    \E c \in Containers :
        /\ lifts[c] = 0
        /\ lifts' = [lifts EXCEPT ![c] = 1]
        /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Reassign ==
    /\ epoch' = IF epoch = MaxEpoch THEN 0 ELSE epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED lifts

Next == NormalLift \/ AdminForceLift \/ Reassign

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LiftedAtMostOnce == \A c \in Containers : lifts[c] <= 1
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Containers = {c1, c2, c3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LiftedAtMostOnce
nl:
A container-ship crane yard lifts containers off a vessel, and each physical container may be lifted exactly one time before it leaves the yard. The gantry cranes are reassigned in numbered epochs as the load plan changes, and within an epoch a crane picks a container that has not yet been lifted and lifts it, marking it done. There is also a privileged yard supervisor who holds an admin override: the supervisor can force a lift on any not-yet-lifted container regardless of the current crane assignment. Whether a lift happens through the normal epoch mechanism or through the admin override, the same physical rule applies: a container that has already been lifted must never be lifted again. We track a per-container lift count as the ground truth.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no container is ever lifted more than once, so every container's lift count stays at zero or one.

spec_text:
--------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m5p3t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Drones, Slots, Council, Quorum

ASSUME Council \in Nat /\ Quorum \in Nat

VARIABLES holdings, active, approvals

vars == << holdings, active, approvals >>

Owners(s) == { d \in Drones : s \in holdings[d] }

Init ==
    /\ holdings = [d \in Drones |-> {}]
    /\ active = Slots
    /\ approvals = [d \in Drones |-> 0]

Approve ==
    \E d \in Drones :
        /\ approvals[d] < Council
        /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![d] = @ + 1]
        /\ UNCHANGED << holdings, active >>

Claim ==
    \E d \in Drones, s \in Slots :
        /\ s \in active
        /\ approvals[d] >= Quorum
        /\ Owners(s) = {}
        /\ holdings' = [holdings EXCEPT ![d] = @ \cup {s}]
        /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
        /\ UNCHANGED active

Release ==
    \E d \in Drones, s \in Slots :
        /\ s \in holdings[d]
        /\ holdings' = [holdings EXCEPT ![d] = @ \ {s}]
        /\ UNCHANGED << active, approvals >>

Deactivate ==
    \E s \in active :
        /\ active' = active \ {s}
        /\ holdings' = [d \in Drones |-> holdings[d] \ {s}]
        /\ UNCHANGED approvals

Activate ==
    \E s \in Slots :
        /\ s \notin active
        /\ active' = active \cup {s}
        /\ UNCHANGED << holdings, approvals >>

Next == Approve \/ Claim \/ Release \/ Deactivate \/ Activate

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation == \A s \in Slots : Cardinality(Owners(s)) <= 1
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {dA, dB}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    Council = 2
    Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A wildfire drone swarm allocates observation slots, where each slot is a specific airspace lane that at most one drone may own at a time. A drone that wants a lane must first gather a quorum of approvals from the mission council; once it has enough approvals it may claim a lane, provided no other drone currently holds that lane. The set of usable lanes changes at runtime: as smoke and wind shift, the operations center activates new lanes or deactivates existing ones, and deactivating a lane strips it from whichever drone held it. Claiming a lane consumes the drone's gathered approvals. The cardinal rule is that the same lane must never be simultaneously owned by two different drones, because that would put two aircraft on a collision course.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no observation lane is ever held by two different drones at the same time.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m0p0t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Cars, Segments, MaxVersion

ASSUME MaxVersion \in Nat

VARIABLES occ, version, snapSeg, snapVer

vars == << occ, version, snapSeg, snapVer >>

Bump(v) == IF v = MaxVersion THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

Init ==
    /\ occ = [s \in Segments |-> {}]
    /\ version = [s \in Segments |-> 0]
    /\ snapSeg = [c \in Cars |-> "none"]
    /\ snapVer = [c \in Cars |-> 0]

Read ==
    \E c \in Cars, s \in Segments :
        /\ snapSeg[c] = "none"
        /\ snapSeg' = [snapSeg EXCEPT ![c] = s]
        /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![c] = version[s]]
        /\ UNCHANGED << occ, version >>

Commit ==
    \E c \in Cars :
        /\ snapSeg[c] # "none"
        /\ LET s == snapSeg[c] IN
            /\ version[s] = snapVer[c]
            /\ occ[s] = {}
            /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![s] = {c}]
            /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = Bump(@)]
        /\ snapSeg' = [snapSeg EXCEPT ![c] = "none"]
        /\ UNCHANGED snapVer

Abort ==
    \E c \in Cars :
        /\ snapSeg[c] # "none"
        /\ LET s == snapSeg[c] IN version[s] # snapVer[c] \/ occ[s] # {}
        /\ snapSeg' = [snapSeg EXCEPT ![c] = "none"]
        /\ UNCHANGED << occ, version, snapVer >>

Leave ==
    \E c \in Cars, s \in Segments :
        /\ c \in occ[s]
        /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![s] = @ \ {c}]
        /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = Bump(@)]
        /\ UNCHANGED << snapSeg, snapVer >>

Next == Read \/ Commit \/ Abort \/ Leave

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SegmentMutualExclusion == \A s \in Segments : Cardinality(occ[s]) <= 1
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carX, carY}
    Segments = {seg1, seg2}
    MaxVersion = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SegmentMutualExclusion
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is driven by two independent dispatch controllers that share one pool of shaft segments. A segment is a critical resource: only one elevator car may occupy a given segment at a time, or cars would collide. Each segment carries a version stamp, and a controller uses optimistic locking to move a car in: it reads the segment's version, and its move only succeeds if the version has not changed in the meantime, at which point it takes the segment and bumps the version. If the version moved underneath it, the controller's attempt is rejected and it retries later. When a car leaves a segment the segment is freed and its version bumps again. Because the two controllers race over the same shared pool, the optimistic check is the only thing preventing a double-occupancy.
SAFETY PROPERTY: each shaft segment is occupied by at most one elevator car at any time.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m7p4t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Instances, Capacity

ASSUME Capacity \in Nat /\ Capacity >= 1

VARIABLES load, snap, want, reading

vars == << load, snap, want, reading >>

Init ==
    /\ load = 0
    /\ snap = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ want = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ reading = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]

Read ==
    \E i \in Instances, a \in 1 .. Capacity :
        /\ ~reading[i]
        /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
        /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![i] = load]
        /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![i] = a]
        /\ UNCHANGED load

CasCommit ==
    \E i \in Instances :
        /\ reading[i]
        /\ load = snap[i]
        /\ load + want[i] <= Capacity
        /\ load' = load + want[i]
        /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
        /\ UNCHANGED << snap, want >>

CasAbort ==
    \E i \in Instances :
        /\ reading[i]
        /\ (load # snap[i] \/ load + want[i] > Capacity)
        /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
        /\ UNCHANGED << load, snap, want >>

Shed ==
    /\ load > 0
    /\ load' = load - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << snap, want, reading >>

Next == Read \/ CasCommit \/ CasAbort \/ Shed

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LoadWithinCapacity == load <= Capacity
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {i1, i2}
    Capacity = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LoadWithinCapacity
nl:
A power-grid load shedder protects a substation whose total dispatched load must never exceed a hard thermal capacity. Two independent shedder instances share one pool and coordinate through a single compare-and-swap register that holds the current total load. To add load, an instance reads the register into a local snapshot, decides how much extra load to dispatch, and then attempts a compare-and-swap: the write commits only if the register still equals its snapshot and the resulting total would stay within capacity, in which case the register is updated. If the register changed underneath it, the attempt is aborted and retried. Either instance may also shed load, decrementing the register. The whole point of the compare-and-swap discipline is that the two racing instances can never jointly push the dispatched load past the capacity ceiling.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total dispatched load recorded in the register never exceeds the thermal capacity.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m5p0t5 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, Signals, Quorum

ASSUME Signals \in Nat /\ Quorum \in Nat

VARIABLES occ, approvals

vars == << occ, approvals >>

InSomeBlock(t) == \E b \in Blocks : t \in occ[b]

Init ==
    /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> {}]
    /\ approvals = [t \in Trains |-> 0]

Approve ==
    \E t \in Trains :
        /\ approvals[t] < Signals
        /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
        /\ UNCHANGED occ

EnterByQuorum ==
    \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks :
        /\ occ[b] = {}
        /\ ~InSomeBlock(t)
        /\ approvals[t] >= Quorum
        /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = {t}]
        /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![t] = 0]

AdminAdmit ==
    \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks :
        /\ occ[b] = {}
        /\ ~InSomeBlock(t)
        /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = {t}]
        /\ UNCHANGED approvals

Leave ==
    \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks :
        /\ t \in occ[b]
        /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = @ \ {t}]
        /\ UNCHANGED approvals

Next == Approve \/ EnterByQuorum \/ AdminAdmit \/ Leave

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BlockMutualExclusion == \A b \in Blocks : Cardinality(occ[b]) <= 1
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Trains = {tr1, tr2}
    Blocks = {b1, b2}
    Signals = 2
    Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BlockMutualExclusion
nl:
A subway signalling system divides a line into track blocks, and a block is a critical resource that at most one train may occupy, or a rear-end collision becomes possible. A train requesting entry to a block must gather a quorum of approvals from the interlocking signals covering that block before the controller admits it, and admission is granted only if the target block is currently clear. A train occupies at most one block at a time. There is also a privileged dispatcher with an admin override who can admit a train into a clear block immediately, bypassing the quorum, for emergency moves. Whether entry comes through quorum or through the override, the block must be clear first. The invariant that keeps trains safe is that no block ever holds two trains.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no track block is ever occupied by two different trains simultaneously.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m7p3t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Robots, Chargers

VARIABLES holder, reading, sawFree

vars == << holder, reading, sawFree >>

Init ==
    /\ holder = [s \in Chargers |-> {}]
    /\ reading = [r \in Robots |-> "none"]
    /\ sawFree = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]

BeginClaim ==
    \E r \in Robots, s \in Chargers :
        /\ reading[r] = "none"
        /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![r] = s]
        /\ sawFree' = [sawFree EXCEPT ![r] = (holder[s] = {})]
        /\ UNCHANGED holder

CasCommit ==
    \E r \in Robots :
        /\ reading[r] # "none"
        /\ sawFree[r]
        /\ holder[reading[r]] = {}
        /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![reading[r]] = {r}]
        /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![r] = "none"]
        /\ sawFree' = [sawFree EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]

CasAbort ==
    \E r \in Robots :
        /\ reading[r] # "none"
        /\ (~sawFree[r] \/ holder[reading[r]] # {})
        /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![r] = "none"]
        /\ sawFree' = [sawFree EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
        /\ UNCHANGED holder

Release ==
    \E r \in Robots, s \in Chargers :
        /\ r \in holder[s]
        /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = @ \ {r}]
        /\ UNCHANGED << reading, sawFree >>

AdminReassign ==
    \E r \in Robots, s \in Chargers :
        /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = {r}]
        /\ UNCHANGED << reading, sawFree >>

Next == BeginClaim \/ CasCommit \/ CasAbort \/ Release \/ AdminReassign

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoSlotDoubleHeld == \A s \in Chargers : Cardinality(holder[s]) <= 1
=============================================================================
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a bank of charging slots, and a slot must never be allocated to two robots at once or the chargers would be damaged. Each slot is guarded by a compare-and-swap register recording its current holder. A robot claims a slot in two steps: it reads whether the slot is free, then attempts a compare-and-swap that succeeds only if the slot is still free at commit time, taking ownership; if another robot grabbed it first, the attempt aborts and the robot retries elsewhere. A robot releases its slot when charged. A privileged fleet supervisor holds an admin override and may forcibly reassign any slot to a chosen robot, which atomically replaces whoever held it. The core guarantee is that a single charging slot never ends up held by two robots simultaneously.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every charging slot is held by at most one robot at any given time.

spec_text:
--------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m9p2t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Total, MaxEpoch

ASSUME Total \in Nat /\ MaxEpoch \in Nat

VARIABLES shelf, reserved, lent, epoch, branchUp

vars == << shelf, reserved, lent, epoch, branchUp >>

Init ==
    /\ shelf = Total
    /\ reserved = 0
    /\ lent = 0
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ branchUp = TRUE

Reserve ==
    /\ shelf > 0
    /\ shelf' = shelf - 1
    /\ reserved' = reserved + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << lent, epoch, branchUp >>

Borrow ==
    /\ branchUp
    /\ reserved > 0
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ lent' = lent + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << shelf, epoch, branchUp >>

ReturnCopy ==
    /\ lent > 0
    /\ lent' = lent - 1
    /\ shelf' = shelf + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << reserved, epoch, branchUp >>

Cancel ==
    /\ reserved > 0
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ shelf' = shelf + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << lent, epoch, branchUp >>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch' = IF epoch = MaxEpoch THEN 0 ELSE epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << shelf, reserved, lent, branchUp >>

CrashOrRecover ==
    /\ branchUp' = ~branchUp
    /\ UNCHANGED << shelf, reserved, lent, epoch >>

Next == Reserve \/ Borrow \/ ReturnCopy \/ Cancel \/ Reconfigure \/ CrashOrRecover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CopiesConserved == shelf + reserved + lent = Total
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Total = 3
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CopiesConserved
nl:
A library reservation system manages a fixed number of copies of a popular title, and every copy is always in exactly one of three states: sitting on the shelf, reserved for a patron, or lent out. Patrons reserve an available copy, later borrow a reserved copy, and eventually return a lent copy to the shelf; a reservation can also be cancelled, returning the copy to the shelf. The reservation service runs across branch nodes, and one branch node can crash silently and stop processing borrows for a while; borrowing is only possible while that branch is up. The catalog reconfigures itself in numbered epochs as policies change. Through all of this, copies are never created or destroyed. The librarian must always be able to reconcile the books: the copies on the shelf, reserved, and lent must add up to the fixed total.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of copies on the shelf plus reserved plus lent always equals the fixed total number of copies.

Several matchmaker nodes stand ready, and exactly one of them acts as the elected leader that is allowed to start matches. A node may be elected leader only when there is no current leader. The leader can crash silently, which clears the leadership and triggers a failover so another live node can be elected. Crashed nodes may later recover. No matter how leadership churns through crashes and re-elections, a given match must be started at most once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m0p1t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS MaxPer, MaxVersion

ASSUME MaxPer \in Nat /\ MaxVersion \in Nat

Bump(v) == IF v = MaxVersion THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

Stations == {"wa", "wb"}

VARIABLES count, tally, ver, snap, reading

vars == << count, tally, ver, snap, reading >>

Init ==
    /\ count = 0
    /\ tally = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ snap = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
    /\ reading = [s \in Stations |-> FALSE]

Read ==
    \E s \in Stations :
        /\ ~reading[s]
        /\ tally[s] < MaxPer
        /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
        /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![s] = ver]
        /\ UNCHANGED << count, tally, ver >>

Commit ==
    \E s \in Stations :
        /\ reading[s]
        /\ ver = snap[s]
        /\ count' = count + 1
        /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
        /\ ver' = Bump(ver)
        /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
        /\ UNCHANGED snap

Abort ==
    \E s \in Stations :
        /\ reading[s]
        /\ ver # snap[s]
        /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
        /\ UNCHANGED << count, tally, ver, snap >>

AdminApply ==
    \E s \in Stations :
        /\ tally[s] < MaxPer
        /\ count' = count + 1
        /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
        /\ ver' = Bump(ver)
        /\ UNCHANGED << snap, reading >>

Retire ==
    \E s \in Stations :
        /\ tally[s] > 0
        /\ count' = count - 1
        /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1]
        /\ ver' = Bump(ver)
        /\ UNCHANGED << snap, reading >>

    MaxVersion = 3
INIT Init

nl:
A car-wash conveyor line keeps a shared throughput record counting how many cars have been fully processed, and each wash station folds its own completions into that record. To stop two stations from clobbering the shared count, the record carries a version stamp and stations use optimistic locking: a station reads the current version, and its increment commits only if the version is unchanged at commit time, at which point it bumps both the shared count and its own per-station tally and advances the version. If the version moved, the station aborts and retries. A privileged line manager holds an admin override that can atomically apply a station's completion directly, updating the shared count and that station's tally together. The books must stay consistent: the shared throughput record must always equal the sum of every station's tally, so no completion is ever lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared throughput count always equals the sum of the per-station completion tallies.

nl:
A university course-registration system enrolls students into a course that has a hard seat capacity. Enrollment is coordinated by a two-phase commit across several registration nodes: a coordinator proposes to seat one more student, each node votes, and the enrollment is committed only if every node votes yes and there is still room under the capacity. If any node votes no, or the coordinator times out, the round aborts and nothing changes. Nodes can crash silently and simply stop voting for a while, later recovering. Seats can also be freed when students drop. The registrar's absolute constraint is that the number of enrolled students must never exceed the course capacity, no matter how votes interleave or nodes crash and recover.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of enrolled students never exceeds the course seat capacity.

The ledger is a single structured record holding a grand total together with a per-controller breakdown. To prevent two controllers from clobbering the total, the controllers form a logical ring and pass a single write token; only the controller holding the token may post a serviced call, which increments both the grand total and its own entry in the breakdown. The ring runs over a flaky link so token handoffs can be reordered and the token may jump to any controller next. The consistency requirement is that the ledger's grand total always equals the sum of the per-controller entries, so no serviced call is ever lost or double-counted in the total.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m9p3t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Controllers, Zones, MaxEpoch

ASSUME MaxEpoch \in Nat

VARIABLES grants, owner, active, epoch

vars == << grants, owner, active, epoch >>

Init ==
    /\ grants = [z \in Zones |-> 0]
    /\ owner = [z \in Zones |-> "free"]
    /\ active = Zones
    /\ epoch = 0

Grant ==
    \E z \in Zones, c \in Controllers :
        /\ z \in active
        /\ grants[z] = 0
        /\ grants' = [grants EXCEPT ![z] = @ + 1]
        /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![z] = c]
        /\ UNCHANGED << active, epoch >>

Release ==
    \E z \in Zones :
        /\ grants[z] > 0
        /\ grants' = [grants EXCEPT ![z] = @ - 1]
        /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![z] = "free"]
        /\ UNCHANGED << active, epoch >>

Deactivate ==
    \E z \in active :
        /\ active' = active \ {z}
        /\ grants' = [grants EXCEPT ![z] = 0]
        /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![z] = "free"]
        /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Activate ==
    \E z \in Zones :
        /\ z \notin active
        /\ active' = active \cup {z}
        /\ UNCHANGED << grants, owner, epoch >>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch' = IF epoch = MaxEpoch THEN 0 ELSE epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << grants, owner, active >>

The safety concern is that no zone is ever simultaneously controlled by two different controllers, which would create conflicting lock commands.

Election and release messages travel over a fabric that can reorder them, so elections resolve in arbitrary order.     /\ acting
    /\ acting' = FALSE
    /\ actor' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, expiry, clock >>

    /\ owner' = "none"
    /\ acting' = FALSE
    /\ actor' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED << expiry, clock >>

nl:
A multiplayer game lobby is managed by two independent server instances that share one pool of lobbies, coordinated by a lease with an expiry. At any moment at most one server holds the lease, acquired when the lobby is unowned or the previous lease has expired against the clock. Only the server that currently holds a valid, unexpired lease is authorized to act on the lobby, such as admitting players or starting the countdown. When the lease is handed to a new owner or explicitly released, any previously acting server must stop, because it is no longer authorized. The safety requirement is that whenever a server is acting on the lobby, it is the current lease owner and not some stale or unauthorized participant.

    /\ UNCHANGED << queue, belt >>

Assignments are made by an elected leader controller: a node may grant a block to a train only while it is the current leader, and a grant is allowed only if the target train currently holds no block and the block is not already assigned to another train. nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler governs one operating room that only a single surgical team may occupy, and admission is decided by a two-phase commit across the scheduling board. A team proposing to enter must collect a yes vote from every board member; if all members vote yes and the room is currently empty, the commit admits the team. Board members can crash silently and stop voting for a while, later recovering, and the coordinator may abort a round at any time, clearing the votes. A team leaves when its procedure ends, freeing the room. The non-negotiable safety property is that two different surgical teams are never in the operating room at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no two surgical teams are ever in the operating room simultaneously.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m1p3t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Instances, Slots, Patients

VARIABLES booked, token

vars == << booked, token >>

Init ==
    /\ booked = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
    /\ token \in Instances

BookSlot ==
    \E i \in Instances, s \in Slots, p \in Patients :
        /\ token = i
        /\ booked[s] = {}
        /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![s] = {p}]
        /\ UNCHANGED token

Cancel ==
    \E s \in Slots, p \in Patients :
        /\ p \in booked[s]
        /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![s] = @ \ {p}]
        /\ UNCHANGED token

PassToken ==
    \E j \in Instances :
        /\ j # token
        /\ token' = j
        /\ UNCHANGED booked

Next == BookSlot \/ Cancel \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoSlotDoubleBooked == \A s \in Slots : Cardinality(booked[s]) <= 1
=============================================================================
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler books time slots for surgeries, drawing requests from two independent scheduling instances that share one pool of slots. To serialize bookings, the instances form a logical ring and pass a single booking token; only the instance holding the token may book a slot, and it may book a slot for a patient only if that slot is currently unbooked. A booking can later be cancelled, freeing the slot. Because both instances draw from the same shared pool of slots, the token discipline is what prevents them from booking the same slot for two different patients. The safety property is that no time slot is ever booked for two different patients at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no operating-room time slot is ever booked for two different patients at the same time.
